quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: ____ the museum was completely free to enter, hardly anyone showed up on opening day.
quests.sentence: ____ the museum was completely free to enter, hardly anyone showed up on opening day.
quests.hint: This concession clause opens the sentence - which connector can grammatically start a sentence like this?
quests.explanation: 'Although' can introduce a concession clause at the very start of a sentence. 'But' and 'yet' link two independent clauses and can't be used to open a sentence this way.
quests.grammarRule: Concession - although (structural: can front, unlike but/yet)

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: The soup needed more salt, ____ nobody at the table wanted to say anything.
quests.sentence: The soup needed more salt, ____ nobody at the table wanted to say anything.
quests.hint: This is a casual, everyday observation - the neutral, mid-sentence contrast word fits best here.
quests.explanation: 'But' is the natural, everyday choice for this casual contrast. 'Although' would also be grammatically fine here but sounds slightly more formal than this relaxed remark calls for.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: ____ the goalkeeper had never played in a championship match before, she made three incredible saves in the final.
quests.sentence: ____ the goalkeeper had never played in a championship match before, she made three incredible saves in the final.
quests.hint: This concession clause opens the sentence - only certain connectors can start a sentence this way.
quests.explanation: 'Although' introduces this concession at the sentence's start. 'But' can't be used to open a sentence like this.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: ____ international sales grew by twelve percent last year, domestic sales remained essentially flat.
quests.sentence: ____ international sales grew by twelve percent last year, domestic sales remained essentially flat.
quests.hint: This reads like a formal business report comparing two different figures side by side.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' formally compares these two contrasting sales trends. 'Although' would suggest one trend happened despite some obstacle, which isn't the relationship here.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: My roommate loves getting up at dawn to jog, ____ I can barely function before ten.
quests.sentence: My roommate loves getting up at dawn to jog, ____ I can barely function before ten.
quests.hint: This is a casual, everyday comparison between two people's habits, not a formal report.
quests.explanation: 'While' compares these two contrasting habits in everyday speech, much like 'whereas' does more formally. 'Because' would incorrectly suggest one habit causes the other.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: Some nutritionists recommend eating six small meals a day, ____ others insist three balanced meals are just as effective.
quests.sentence: Some nutritionists recommend eating six small meals a day, ____ others insist three balanced meals are just as effective.
quests.hint: Two different professional opinions are simply being compared here, with neither happening despite the other.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' compares these two contrasting recommendations. 'Because' would incorrectly suggest one opinion causes the other.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: The hike sounds exhausting ____ I think I'll still come along.
quests.sentence: The hike sounds exhausting ____ I think I'll still come along.
quests.hint: This is a relaxed, spoken-style message - the more casual of the near-identical concession connectors fits better here.
quests.explanation: 'Though' feels natural in this casual tone. 'Because' would incorrectly frame the second clause as the reason the hike sounds exhausting.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: ____ she'd broken her ankle just two weeks earlier, Elena insisted on walking across the stage at graduation.
quests.sentence: ____ she'd broken her ankle just two weeks earlier, Elena insisted on walking across the stage at graduation.
quests.hint: A broken ankle just two weeks prior is a serious obstacle - this deserves the stronger of these two near-identical connectors.
quests.explanation: 'Even though' emphasizes the significant obstacle she overcame. 'Although' would also technically work, but doesn't carry quite the same weight of emphasis given how recent and serious the injury was.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: ____ the initial survey results were inconclusive, the research team decided to publish their preliminary findings.
quests.sentence: ____ the initial survey results were inconclusive, the research team decided to publish their preliminary findings.
quests.hint: This reads like a formal research report - which of the near-identical connectors fits that more formal tone better?
quests.explanation: 'Although' suits this formal, written register. 'Though' means the same thing but tends to feel more conversational, less fitting for a research report.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: The underdog team had lost every game that season, ____ they somehow made it to the finals.
quests.sentence: The underdog team had lost every game that season, ____ they somehow made it to the finals.
quests.hint: Making the finals despite a losing streak is the surprising part - a concession-like twist expressed with the everyday contrast word.
quests.explanation: 'But' captures this unexpected turnaround. 'Whereas' would only fit for comparing two separate, parallel facts, not this kind of surprising reversal.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: Downtown parking rates rise sharply during rush hour, ____ suburban lots charge a flat rate all day.
quests.sentence: Downtown parking rates rise sharply during rush hour, ____ suburban lots charge a flat rate all day.
quests.hint: Two different pricing systems are simply being compared here, with neither being an unexpected twist.
quests.explanation: 'Whereas' compares these two contrasting pricing structures. 'But' would work too but sounds less suited to this precise, informational comparison.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: The recipe looked complicated on paper, ____ it only took Ben twenty minutes to make.
quests.sentence: The recipe looked complicated on paper, ____ it only took Ben twenty minutes to make.
quests.hint: The dish being quicker than expected is the pleasant surprise here.
quests.explanation: 'But' captures this unexpected ease. 'Whereas' would only fit for comparing two separate, parallel facts, not this kind of surprising twist.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.
quests.question: The clinic extended its hours this month ____ demand for flu shots had spiked unexpectedly.
quests.sentence: The clinic extended its hours this month ____ demand for flu shots had spiked unexpectedly.
quests.hint: This explains the actual reason for the extended hours, not a contrast or comparison.
quests.explanation: 'Because' gives the direct reason behind the extended hours. 'Although' or 'whereas' would incorrectly frame this as some kind of contrast rather than a straightforward cause.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: The professor posted lecture slides in advance ____ students could prepare questions beforehand.
quests.sentence: The professor posted lecture slides in advance ____ students could prepare questions beforehand.
quests.hint: This was a deliberate step taken with a specific future goal in mind.
quests.explanation: 'So that' introduces this intentional purpose, with 'could' expressing the enabled benefit. 'Because' would incorrectly frame this as an explanation rather than a forward-looking goal.

quests.explanation: 'Although' shows the concession between her negative impression and the positive outcome. 'Whereas' would only fit for comparing two separate, parallel facts, not this kind of surprising reversal.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.
quests.question: The evidence against the defendant seemed overwhelming, ____ the jury returned a verdict of not guilty.
quests.sentence: The evidence against the defendant seemed overwhelming, ____ the jury returned a verdict of not guilty.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.
quests.question: ____ the new policy was designed to reduce paperwork, most employees say it actually created more.
quests.sentence: ____ the new policy was designed to reduce paperwork, most employees say it actually created more.

quests.explanation: 'Although' captures this concession between the policy's intended goal and its actual, disappointing effect. 'Whereas' would only fit for comparing two separate, parallel facts side by side.
quests.grammarRule: Concession vs Contrast - although, not whereas

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that fits best.

quests.sentence: My sister is really into true crime podcasts ____ I honestly can't stand them.

quests.explanation: 'While' compares these two contrasting preferences in a natural, everyday way. 'Though' would suggest something happening despite an obstacle, which isn't quite this simple comparison of tastes.

quests.instruction: Select the connector that best completes the sentence.

quests.sentence: ____ the company had cut its marketing budget in half, sales actually increased that quarter.

quests.explanation: 'Even though' emphasizes this strong, surprising concession. 'Whereas' would only fit for comparing two separate, parallel facts, not this kind of dramatic reversal.

quests.instruction: Choose the connector that correctly links the two clauses.
quests.question: The bank will freeze the account automatically ____ the missing paperwork is submitted within a week.
quests.sentence: The bank will freeze the account automatically ____ the missing paperwork is submitted within a week.
quests.hint: Freezing happens specifically when the paperwork does NOT get submitted in time - which connector already includes that 'not'?
quests.explanation: 'Unless' shows the freeze depends on the paperwork failing to arrive in time. 'Because' would incorrectly frame this as an explanation rather than a condition.

quests.instruction: Complete the sentence with the best connector.

quests.hint: Her determination holds true no matter what her parents think - stronger than a simple condition.
quests.explanation: 'Even if' shows her plans stay firm regardless of their possible disapproval. 'Although' would only work if their disapproval had already definitely happened.
